steps.name: Prepare ranked gene list from DESeq2 results
steps.question: Does the provided de_results.csv (treated vs control, psoriasis lesional vs skin control, 12000 genes) give a clean, uniquely-mapped ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald 'stat') for every tested gene, with duplicates and NAs resolved, suitable as fgsea preranked input?

grounding.reason: Ranking metric for preranked GSEA on DESeq2 output is the Wald statistic, not unshrunken log2FC or a signed p-value with ties (R-0099); the full tested-gene list is used, not a thresholded one (R-0045).

steps.description: Load de_results.csv, verify columns (gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change shrunken, stat/Wald statistic, p-value, padj), drop genes with NA stat (DESeq2 outlier/independent-filtering NAs), collapse duplicate gene symbols (keep the entry with the largest |stat| or mean if duplicated), and produce a named numeric vector of stat values ranked descending. Report the number of input genes (12000), the number dropped for NA, the number of duplicate symbols collapsed, and the final ranked list size. This is the exact tested-gene universe used later as the enrichment universe.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked vector written with one value per unique gene symbol, no NAs, no duplicate names
Counts of dropped/collapsed genes reported explicitly
Ranking metric documented as the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column)

steps.name: fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways are significantly enriched (up or down) in psoriasis-lesional vs control skin, based on the DESeq2 Wald-statistic-ranked gene list?

grounding.reason: fgsea preranked GSEA on MSigDB Hallmark is the default first-pass enrichment for a human dataset with a full ranked list (R-0107, R-0048); size window 15-500 (R-0047); collapse redundant sets before reporting (R-0052); ranking-statistic choice (Wald stat) stated per the disputed rule R-0108.

steps.description: Run fgsea::fgseaMultilevel (preranked GSEA) on the ranked gene list from T1S1 against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols, at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt). Restrict to gene sets with 15-500 members after intersecting with the tested-gene universe. Use Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the 50 tested Hallmark sets. Report normalized enrichment score (NES), p-value, padj, set size, and leading-edge genes for every set; flag sets at padj < 0.05 as significant. Collapse any highly redundant significant hallmark sets (fgsea::collapsePathways) and note which representative set each redundant group maps to. Set and record a random seed for permutation reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run against all 50 Hallmark sets with the 15-500 gene size window applied post-intersection
Output table has NES, pval, padj, size, leadingEdge per pathway
Random seed recorded; collapsed/redundant pathway groups reported

steps.name: fgsea preranked GSEA against Reactome pathways (follow-up)
steps.question: For the Hallmark sets found significant in T2S1, which specific Reactome pathways (curated, hierarchical) resolve or corroborate the broad hallmark signature in psoriasis-lesional vs control skin?

grounding.reason: For human data, Reactome is the stated second enrichment collection after Hallmark, resolving a hallmark hit to specific curated pathways.

steps.description: Run the same fgsea preranked analysis (same ranked list from T1S1, same 15-500 gene size window, same BH adjustment within this collection) against the Reactome human pathway gene sets (present at /mnt/refs/managed/reactome-pathways/current/ReactomePathways.gmt; restrict to Homo sapiens using the accompanying ReactomePathways.txt index, since the GMT covers all species). Report NES, padj, size, and leading-edge genes for significant Reactome pathways, and note the overlap between genes driving significant Reactome pathways and genes driving the corresponding significant Hallmark sets from T2S1, to show which specific mechanisms underlie each broad hallmark hit.
acceptance_criteria: ReactomePathways.gmt filtered to Homo sapiens via ReactomePathways.txt before testing
fgsea output includes NES/padj/size/leadingEdge per significant Reactome pathway
Overlap between Reactome and Hallmark leading-edge gene sets reported for shared biology

steps.name: Enrichment report: significant hallmark pathways with reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the final, reported set of Hallmark pathways that change between psoriasis-lesional and control skin, with what supporting evidence and what caveats?

grounding.reason: Report step must state database/version/ranking metric/universe/size window (R-0051), the method-dependence caveat (R-0055), leading-edge genes per significant set (R-0105), and a full reproducibility record (R-0086).

steps.description: Synthesize T2S1 (Hallmark) and T2S2 (Reactome follow-up) into one report: table of significant Hallmark pathways (padj<0.05) with NES, direction (up in lesional vs control), size, and leading-edge genes; the collapsed/redundant groupings from T2S1; the corroborating Reactome pathways for each significant hallmark hit; and a p-value histogram diagnostic of the DE result's stat/p-value distribution feeding the ranking. State explicitly: the gene set database and version (MSigDB Hallmark 2026.1, Reactome current), the ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic), the universe (12000 tested genes from de_results.csv, minus NA-stat exclusions), the size window (15-500), the multiple-testing method (BH), that fgsea significance is method-dependent (a different ranking metric or ORA on a thresholded list could give a different set of significant pathways), and that sample_01's ~4x-below-median library depth was already accounted for via DESeq2 size factors in the upstream DE step, not re-corrected here. Include the fgsea/R sessionInfo, the permutation seed, and gene-set collection version numbers as the reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: Final table of significant Hallmark pathways with NES, direction, padj, leading-edge genes
Reactome corroboration cross-referenced per hallmark hit
Report explicitly states database version, ranking metric, universe, size window, multiple-testing method, and method-dependence caveat
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seed, package/collection versions) included
Caveat on sample_01 library depth stated relative to the upstream DE step

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control: Hallmark pathway GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The DE step (DESeq2, treated vs control, 6 vs 6) is already complete and provided as de_results.csv (12000 genes x 8 columns including stat, log2FoldChange, padj). The research question asks specifically which hallmark pathways change between psoriasis-lesional (treated) and control skin. Per the grounded procedure (fgsea preranked GSEA, R-0107/R-0045/R-0099), the correct approach given an existing full DE results table is to rank every tested gene by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column) and run fgsea preranked against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (50 sets, present at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt). A Reactome follow-up pass (present at /mnt/refs/managed/reactome-pathways/current/ReactomePathways.gmt) resolves any hallmark hit to specific curated pathways, per R-0098. No new DE modeling, filtering, or normalization step is needed since de_results.csv already carries the DESeq2 Wald statistic for every tested gene — this plan begins directly at gene identifier mapping/QC of the ranking input and proceeds to enrichment and reporting. The caveat about sample_01's low library depth is inherited from the already-completed DE step (DESeq2's size-factor normalization already accounts for it per R-0030) and is carried into the report rather than re-litigated.

steps.method: fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic (stat column from DESeq2 results)
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with Reactome pathways (follow-up)
Enrichment summary report with leading-edge genes and reproducibility record
